guarantees.claim: block_processed_o is continuously assigned the value of keccak_complete.
state_valid_o is continuously assigned the value of state_valid.
state_o is continuously assigned the value of state_guarded.
sha3_fsm_o is continuously assigned the result of sparse2logic(st).
The macro PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM instantiates a state register that updates st with st_d on each clock edge and resets to StIdle_sparse.
guarantees.cond: on positive clock edge (inferred from macro name)

assumptions.claim: keccak_complete must be glitch-free and meet the timing requirements of the consumer of block_processed_o.
assumptions.risk: glitches could cause false block_processed indications downstream.

assumptions.claim: st_d must be a valid sparse one-hot encoding consistent with sha3_st_sparse_e at every clock edge.
assumptions.risk: the sparse flop may capture an illegal state, leading to undefined FSM behavior.

uncertain_points.claim: state_guarded is directly assigned to state_o; it is unclear whether state_guarded contains secret or sensitive cryptographic material that should not be exposed without additional masking or filtering.
uncertain_points.risk: if state_guarded holds unprotected secrets (e.g., key bits, digest intermediates), they will be observable at state_o, breaking confidentiality.

uncertain_points.claim: The PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM macro may not explicitly handle illegal non-one-hot inputs on st_d (e.g., due to glitches or soft errors); the resulting st could represent an undefined state.
uncertain_points.cond: if st_d becomes multi-bit or zero
uncertain_points.risk: FSM could enter a dead-end, skip security-critical stages, or produce incorrect outputs without detection.

uncertain_points.claim: The behavior of sparse2logic on an illegal sparse input from st (e.g., if the flop captures a faulty value) is not specified here; the output sha3_fsm_o may become an invalid logical state.
uncertain_points.cond: if st is not a one-hot sparse value
uncertain_points.risk: sha3_fsm_o could assert an inconsistent or reserved value, confusing external monitors or causing false state reports.
